item.title: Food processing influences metabolism and brain activity
item.description:
📝 Neuroscientist Alex DiFeliceantonio (left) and researcher Zach Hutelin at Virginia Tech’s Fralin Biomedical Research Institute at VTC unexpectedly found that two meals with the same carbohydrates, fats, proteins, water, calories, salt, and weight — but that differed in their level of processing — produced different brain and metabolic responses. Researchers exploring that question were surprised to find that minimally and highly processed meals nutritionally matched on calories, carbohydrates, fats, proteins, water, salt, and weight produced distinct metabolic responses. Photos courtesy Zach Hutelin.
🔗 Read more: https://news.vt.edu/articles/2026/10/research_fralinbiomed_upfhutelin.html
